objective: Prove a safe degree-two suppression reduction with explicit changed parameters and audit strict low-density boundary cases without removing K1 from the root.

atomic_claims.text: A triangle-free no-MC graph of order at least two has average degree at least 12/5; K(2,3) audits equality.
At girth at least five, suppressing degree-two vertices of a 2-connected no-MC graph gives a simple 2-connected no-MC graph of minimum degree at least three and girth at least ceil(g/2).
Every component of the unmarked core has at least g-3 vertices, by an explicit matching-cut construction for a smaller component.
For 2<d<4 and g>=5 the suppressed graph has average degree strictly below [4+2(d-2)/(g-3)]/(4-d).
On n>=2, average degree <(8g-20)/(3g-7) and girth >=g>=5 suffice for MC; for d=5/2 the least sufficient integer girth is five.

assumptions: The original finite-simple-graph and nonempty-shore semantics are unchanged; all positive subsidiary claims explicitly require n>=2.
C01/C02 supply the explicit cuts and density-preserving 2-connected reduction.
The suppression parameter map assumes 2<d<4 and g>=5; only elementary graph counting and real arithmetic are used.
risks: Source-domain ambiguity remains nonterminal and both obligations remain open.
Suppression preserves neither density nor girth unchanged; girth four can yield parallel edges.
No optimal general density range or novelty is claimed; comparison with the known extremal theorem is pending.
No mathematical verification command or graph enumeration was executed.
